summary: Jules Brooks Levinson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia in 1994, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins and several traditional teachers. He was an assistant professor of religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was a historian educated at Lycée Charlemagne. He held teaching posts at the École Normale Supérieure, served at the Archives nationales (1830–1851), and was professor of history at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

Jules Oppert (1825–1905) worked in linguistics, archaeology, and Iranian studies. Educated at Heidelberg, Bonn, Berlin, and Kiel (Ph.D. 1847), he taught Sanskrit at INALCO and served as professor at the Collège de France and University of Paris from 1874 to 1905.

Julia A. B. Hegewald (born 1971) is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. She earned a BA and a PhD in the history of Indian architecture from SOAS, an MA from Oxford, and completed her habilitation at RWTH Aachen University (2005–2008).

Julia Ching (1934–2001) specialized in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and the Australian National University (Ph.D.). After teaching at Columbia and Yale, she became a professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

Julia F. Andrews (born 1951) is a sinologist and art historian. She completed her studies at Brown University, UC Berkeley, and Harvard University (1976–1984), and joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.
Julia Leslie (1948–2004) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1990 to 2004.
Julian Schott is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. In 2026, he is attested as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg and a faculty member at the University of Vienna.

Julian Strube (born 1985) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. After completing his habilitation at Heidelberg, he held posts at Münster, Hamburg, and the University of Vienna (2021–2024), before becoming chair of religious studies at the University of Göttingen in 2024.

Juliane Schober specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and served as an associate professor (attested 2007) and professor of religious studies (attested 1997) at Arizona State University.

Julie A. Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Frank E. Reynolds. She held an attested post at Miami University in 2011.

Julius Eggeling (1842–1918) was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as secretary to the Royal Asiatic Society, taught Sanskrit at University College London, and was professor at Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting (1839–1913) was a scholar of linguistics and archaeology who studied at Tübingen under Ernst Heinrich Meier and Rudolf von Roth. He served as director of the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire (1871; 1900–1909) and professor at the University of Strasbourg from 1880.

Julius Grill (1840–1930) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen and Jena, completing his doctorate under Rudolf von Roth, and served as professor of Old Testament exegesis at the University of Tübingen from 1888 to 1913.

Julius Jolly (1849–1932) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Munich, Berlin, Leipzig, and Würzburg under Martin Haug and Albrecht Weber, and served as a professor at the University of Würzburg from 1877 to 1920.

Julius Lipner (born 1946) is a scholar of Indology and religion. He studied at Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, Jadavpur, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis. After teaching at Birmingham, he was professor of Hinduism at the University of Cambridge (1975–2013).

Julius Mohl (1800–1876) was a scholar of Iranian and Chinese studies. He studied at Tübingen and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf, later serving as professor of Persian at the Collège de France (1847–1876).

Julius Müller (1801–1878) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Breslau, Göttingen, and Berlin, and held academic posts at the University of Göttingen, the University of Marburg, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1839–1878).

Julius Pokorny (1887–1970) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Rudolf Much at the University of Vienna. He held faculty posts at Vienna, Humboldt University of Berlin (1920–1935), the University of Bern, and the University of Zurich (1944–1970).
Julius Schubring (1839–1914) pursued university studies at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1857–1858), the University of Bonn (~1858–1860), and the University of Göttingen (~1860–1862).
